Section 3: Configuring and Verifying NTP Synchronization
To ensure consistent log timestamps across all network devices, configure NTP: 1. Configure primary
NTP server: ntp server 192.168.1.100 prefer use-vrf management 2. Specify NTP source interface: ntp
source-interface mgmt0 3. Enable NTP authentication if required: ntp authentication-key 1 md5
Cisco123 4. Verify NTP synchronization status: show ntp peer-status 5. Verify detailed clock
synchronization: show ntp status Output must display 'NTP server synchronized' and stratum level 2 or
lower.
Section 4: Disabling Unsecure HTTP and HTTPS Access
For enterprise security hardening, unsecure Web / HTTP management must be disabled: 1. Disable
HTTP server feature: no feature http 2. Disable unsecure HTTP server: no ip http server 3. Disable
secure HTTPS web management (if required): no ip http secure-server 4. Disable NX-API web server:
no feature nxapi 5. Verify feature state: show feature | include http Verification Output must confirm
HTTP feature is disabled ('disabled').

context:
Cisco NX-OS System Management Configuration
Guide
Section 1: Overview of System Management Features
Cisco NX-OS System Management features provide enterprise control for configuring, monitoring, and
maintaining network devices. Key features include: - Secure Shell (SSH) and Telnet management
protocols - Network Time Protocol (NTP) time synchronization across distributed data center switches -
Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP v2c/v3) monitoring and trap generation - Web-based
management access via HTTP and HTTPS (Cisco NX-API) - System Logging (Syslog) and telemetry
streaming - AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) via RADIUS and TACACS+
Section 2: Configuring SSH (Secure Shell)
To configure SSH on Cisco NX-OS switches, perform the following steps: 1. Enable the SSH feature:
feature ssh 2. Generate RSA host key pair: crypto key generate rsa force label ssh-key 2048 3. Restrict
SSH to protocol version 2: ip ssh version 2 4. Verify SSH server status: show ssh server Note:
Disabling Telnet (no feature telnet) is mandatory for enterprise compliance.
